 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 22-10-2022 at about 5.30 p.m., the petitioner was riding a bicycle from his agricultural land towards his home in Chinya, on the left side of the road.

At that time, the respondent No.2, being the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-ES-9424,
rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bicycle of the petitioner from opposite direction.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Taluk General Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he took treatment as in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, the petitioner was working as farmer and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The Nagamangala Rural Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the rider of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsels.
But, they did not choose to file their written statements.
4. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.
On the other hand, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
5. The following points arise for my consideration:
POINTS 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 22- Javaregowda vs Thirthegowda on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56646492/
2 10-2022 at about 5.30 p.m., near Chinya Village, Honakere Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-02- ES-9424 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.
I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and perused the entire material on record.

7. My findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1: Affirmative Point No.2: Partly Affirmative Point No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 8. Point No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 22-10-2022 at about 5.30 p.m., he was riding a bicycle from his agricultural land towards his home at Chinya, on the left side of the road.

At that time, the respondent No.2, being the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-ES-9424, rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bicycle of the petitioner from opposite direction.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as farmer and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
9. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 11 documents as Ex.
P.1 to

11 . Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazer, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.5 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is true copy of charge- sheet, Ex.P.7 is in-patient book of Victoria Hospital, Ex.P.8 is discharge summary of Prashanth Hospital, Ex.P.9 is are medical bills (total 32), Ex.P.10 are prescriptions and Ex.P.11 is notarized copy of Aadhar card.
10. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-ES-9424 and dashing the same to the bicycle of the petitioner from opposite direction.

Further it reveals that, due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his right leg and simple injuries on his left hand and face and other parts of the body.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report, which is marked as Ex.P.6 that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA- 02-ES-9424.

Javaregowda vs Thirthegowda on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56646492/
3 11.

The above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the respondents No.1 and 2, who are the owner and rider of offending vehicle bearing No.KA-02-ES-9424 respectively, as they did not choose to file their written statements and contest the case of petitioner.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-ES-9424 and dashing the same to oncoming bicycle of the petitioner and due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his right leg and other parts of the body.

There is absolutely no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record, which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to negligence of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

12. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the accident has taken place on the left side of 15 feet wide Gangavadi-Chinya road, near Chinya Village, Honakere Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, in between the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-ES-9424 and oncoming bicycle of the petitioner.
As per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report, which is marked as Ex.P.6 that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-02-ES- 9424.
There is no evidence on record to show that, the said final report/charge-sheet has been challenged by the rider or owner of the offending motorcycle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No. KA-02-ES- 9424, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

13. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 in-patient book of Victoria Hospital and Ex.P.8 discharge summary it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered head injury with fracture right fibular right leg cellulitis/injury to right knee with ligament tear.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

14. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held

4 of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

16. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, occurred on 22-10-2022 at about 5.30 p.m., on Gangavadi-Chinya road, near Chinya Village, Honakere Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk,
Mandya District, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-ES-9424. Hence, I answer point No.1 in Affirmative.
17. Point No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-ES-9424 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained head injury with fracture right fibular right leg cellulitis/injury to right knee with ligament tear.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident, he was working as farmer and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his learning capacity.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined any doctor to establish that, due to above injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby he has lost his earning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation to the petitioner under the head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability, does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
ii) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 32 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the bills at serial No.21 and 28 are already included in final bill at serial No.30.
Therefore, the said bills are not taken into consideration.
Hence, the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.41,382/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.41,382/- under the head of medical expenses.

Javaregowda vs Thirthegowda on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56646492/
5 iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. head injury with fracture right fibular right leg cellulitis/injury to right knee with ligament tear.
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days from 25-10-2022 to 27-10-2022, in Prashanth Hospital, Bengaluru.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days in Prashanth Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent some amount towards attendant charges during the said period.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.1000 x 3 = Rs.3,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days in Prashanth Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent some amount towards food and nourishment during the said period.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.800 x 3 = Rs.2,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Chinya Village, Honakere Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, the accident has occurred on Gangavadi-Chinya road, near Chinya Village, Honakere Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk,
Mandya District and he has taken treatment at Prashanth Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as farmer and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do work and continue his avocation.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as farmer and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.

But, as the petitioner himself has asserted in the petition and the same is deposed in his evidence that,
before accident he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, the same is considered as the monthly income of the petitioner.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 3 days as in-patient at Prashanth Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries caused to him.
It might have taken one month period for complete healing of the wounds.

Therefore,
Javaregowda vs Thirthegowda on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56646492/
6 compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.

sentences.text: viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 73 years and unfortunately he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for 3 days as in-patient in Prashanth Hospital, Bengaluru.
It might have taken one month period for complete healing of the wounds.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that,

awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/-
towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that he requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

18. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income -Nil- 2.
Medical expenses 41,382-00 3. Pain and sufferings 30,000-00 4. Attendant charges 3,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 2,400-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 15,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses -Nil-

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,21,782/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
19. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the rider of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider/respondent No.2 of Javaregowda vs Thirthegowda on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56646492/
7 offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-ES-9424 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused to the petitioner by his said vehicle.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,21,782/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer point No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
20. Point No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,21,782/- (Rupees one lakh twenty one thousand seven hundred and eighty two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner and he is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,21,782/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
19. Liability:
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused to the petitioner by his said vehicle.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,21,782/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer point No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,21,782/- (Rupees one lakh twenty one thousand seven hundred and eighty two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner and he is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
